title: Hardening tool/function-calling and structured-output parsing after multiple customer escalations
creator: Mariana Lee
description:
Summary:
Multiple customers (ACME Health, FinEdge, LumenDocs) reported production failures when using function/tool-calling and structured output endpoints. Failures include: server-side streaming truncation that left JSON payloads incomplete, SDK-level strict JSON validation rejecting minor deviations (single quotes/trailing commas), and inconsistent behavior between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments due to different gateway sanitization and reverse-proxy settings.

Scope and severity:
- Affects text->function and chat->function flows across deployment modes.
- Symptoms: 502/504 or schema-validation errors surfaced to customers, or silent partial-exec where tool invocation payloads were not executed because parser timed out on incomplete stream.
- Impact: customer-visible outages for workflows that rely on deterministic structured output; two enterprise customers opened escalations citing production incidents (SLA risk).

Reproduction notes (collected from customer repros and internal tests):
1) Long streaming responses where model emits a JSON object across multiple chunks occasionally omit final '}' when gateway chunk-coalescing mismatch occurs. Repro with streaming length > 8k tokens and enable_prefetch on Dedicated cluster.
2) Function-call sequences with quick successive calls (call tool A then tool B in same turn) sometimes arrive as concatenated JSON without delimiter leading SDK to treat them as single blob. Repro with batched requests to dedicated pool.
3) Private deployments behind customer-managed proxies showed header-based trimming of trailing newlines which our streaming-terminator logic relied on, causing parser to hang until timeout.

Root cause analysis (preliminary):
- Multiple contributing factors rather than one bug: (a) streaming boundary detection relied on heuristics (newline/trailing delimiter) that break under certain proxies; (b) server-side sanitizer in Hosted pipeline normalizes quoting which masked issues but Dedicated/Private retain raw model bytes exposing malformed JSON; (c) SDKs implement strict JSON.parse on completed buffer and reject recoverable variations.

Proposed fix strategy (phased):
Phase 1 - Emergency customer mitigation (today):
- Deploy server-side tolerant-preparser that will: accept single quotes, trailing commas, unescaped control chars, and attempt best-effort normalization into valid JSON before schema validation. Feature-flagged and limited to function-calling endpoints. Roll out to Hosted immediately and prepare a Dedicated config toggle. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4213)
- SDK patch: add a non-breaking option to use a tolerant parser (redwood.parsers.tolerant = true) and surface detailed diagnostics rather than throwing. Publish patch for JS/py clients and ship as minor patch. (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/987)

Phase 2 - Robust protocol update (next release):
- Implement explicit chunk framing for function-calling streams: each JSON payload will be prefixed with a length header (or newline-delimited JSON with strict framing). This moves boundary logic out of heuristics and into the protocol. Requires SDK and server changes plus backward compatibility guardrails. Target: runtime-1.22.
- Add server-side streaming-timeout improvements: incremental parser that reports partial parse progress and can request retransmit/fallback to a compact non-stream response.

Phase 3 - Testing, rollout, and preventative measures:
- Build an e2e regression suite simulating proxies, reverse-proxy trimming, streaming chunk reassembly, and multi-call concatenation. Add tests into CI for Hosted/Dedicated/Private matrices.
- Create a canary rollout path for Dedicated customers and a feature flag for Private appliances so customers can opt-in before auto-upgrade.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Tolerant parsing risks masking upstream model-generation bugs; mitigate by logging normalized diffs to an internal telemetry stream and alerting on percent of tolerant fixes per customer.
- Protocol framing introduces backwards compatibility coordination; we will maintain compatibility with older SDKs for one release cycle and emit deprecation warnings.

Telemetry and monitoring:
- Dashboards: new panel for 'tolerant-parser usage' and 'streaming-incomplete events' per customer in Console. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/streaming-issues (internal).
- Alerts: Pager duty rule for >1% of function-calls in production using tolerant parser for >10 minutes.

Links and artifacts:
- Customer tickets: https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/ACME-1122, https://support.redwood.ai/ticket/FE-778
- Postmortem draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Function+calling+streaming+esc+2026-03 (internal)
- Reproducer scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repro-scripts/tree/main/tool-calling-streaming
- Server PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4213
- SDK JS PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/987

Next steps (owners):
- Jonah Patel (assignee): land emergency tolerant-preparser to Hosted and prepare Dedicated config (ETA 2026-03-14).
- Aisha Kumar: cut SDK minor release and coordinate release notes and migration guidance (ETA 2026-03-16).
- Mariana Lee: coordinate customer comms and schedule postmortem with affected customers and CS (ETA 2026-03-15).
- Reliability team: add e2e tests for streaming framing (owner ENG-4730).

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Hosted emergency tolerant-preparser deployed and verified with ACME Health testflows.
- JS and Python SDKs shipped with opt-in tolerant parser and migration docs.
- Regression tests added and green in CI.
- Canary framing protocol RFC approved and timeline set for runtime-1.22.
